data: Second-largest object in the asteroid belt and the brightest asteroid visible from Earth. NASA's Dawn spacecraft orbited Vesta in 2011–2012 en route to Ceres, revealing a giant south-pole impact basin (Rheasilvia) and a layered, differentiated interior — Vesta is structurally a remnant proto-planet that never grew into a planet.
Dawn — NASA, 2011–12 (orbital survey; first detailed images and gravity field)
Vesta is the second-most-massive belt body — its surface is the only main-belt source confirmed for HED meteorites found on Earth.
Vesta orbits at 2.36 AU — inner belt. Its proximity drove Dawn's choice to visit Vesta first (2011), then leave for Ceres (2015).
A planet that almost was — the rocky remnants between Mars and Jupiter that Jupiter's gravity wouldn't let coalesce.
Half the longest diameter of the orbit ellipse — and the single number that sets the orbital period.
